summary.title: Upper/Lower Bench Press Strength — 12 Weeks
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You came in with a 275lb bench press target — I've built the entire program around getting you there. Week 1 is your calibration week — the weights are set conservatively so you can focus on form and give me honest effort ratings after each set. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Upper Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy upper — 5×5 bench at 170lbs, log honestly.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary strength movement — 5×5 at 75% of your 225lb 1RM establishes your Week 1 baseline and gives me honest data to programme your progression from here.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-back and lat development through a horizontal pull — builds the upper back strength that stabilises your shoulder blades during the bench press.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest development through the incline pressing pattern — adds volume to the pecs at a slightly different angle from flat bench.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width and strength through shoulder adduction — complements the horizontal row to give full back coverage this session.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength through the full press range — direct carryover to bench lockout, which is a common sticking point when adding load to your 1RM.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the horizontal pressing volume in this session and keeps your shoulders healthy over a 12-week programme.

sessions.title: Lower Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Calibration lower — 5×5 squat, log your effort honestly today.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral leg strength movement — develops quads, glutes, and core through the full squat pattern. Heavy lower body training supports overall strength and recovery capacity.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — targets the biceps femoris and semitendinosus in a way the RDL hinge pattern cannot fully replicate.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute exercise through hip extension at full range — directly develops glute max strength and size as a complement to the squat pattern above.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability — trains the ability to resist spinal extension under load, which underpins bracing quality in every heavy compound lift.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 5×8 bench at 145lbs, feel every rep.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that develops mid-back thickness and scapular retraction strength — the upper back must be strong and stable to press heavier loads safely.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull with a reverse grip — emphasises the lower lats and biceps through the pull, complementing the horizontal row in this session for full back coverage.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest volume work through the incline pressing angle — adds pec development beyond what flat bench alone delivers across the training week.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep long head isolation through elbow extension — building tricep mass across all three heads contributes directly to your ability to lock out heavier bench press loads.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the brachialis and bicep long head through a neutral grip curl — builds arm thickness and elbow flexor strength that supports pulling movements in this program.

sessions.title: Lower Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — calibrate RDL and glute work, 3 sets each.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that builds hamstring and glute strength through their full range of motion — the posterior chain emphasis here complements Tuesday's quad-dominant squat session.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Glute-dominant hip extension exercise — maximises glute activation and volume on this posterior-chain focused day without additional spinal loading from a squat pattern.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion at a stretched starting position — the seated variation provides a longer muscle length stimulus than lying leg curl, adding quality volume.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Glute medius isolation through hip abduction — develops the lateral glute that stabilises the hip and knee during single-leg phases of squats and hinges.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that demands full-body tension from the abs, lats, and hip flexors — a progression from the plank that builds the bracing strength needed under a heavy bar.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Direct plantar flexion work — builds lower leg mass and ankle stability, rounding out lower body development on this volume day.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral horizontal pull that allows each side to work through full range independently — trains the lat and mid-back with greater stretch than bilateral rows and identifies and corrects strength imbalances between sides.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Braced arm isolates the short head of the bicep and eliminates all shoulder swing — the most targeted bicep isolation exercise available, ideal as a volume finisher for peak contraction and complete arm development.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist rotational force — complements the anti-extension Ab Wheel work done on Wednesday and builds core stability that transfers to all compound lifts.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust provides a fixed arc and consistent glute loading — on this posterior day it acts as the primary glute compound, directly developing the priority glute muscle group with less setup than the barbell version.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral hinge that trains each hamstring independently while also demanding hip stability and balance — identifies and corrects asymmetries between legs and adds quality hamstring volume as part of the priority muscle development target.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Priority quad movement added to this posterior session because quads are a priority muscle group — leg press adds quad volume without the spinal demands of a squat, maintaining the priority development target across the full week.

exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — targets the biceps femoris and semitendinosus directly in a way the hip hinge pattern on Tuesday does not fully replicate.

sessions.title: Chest & Back Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline upper heavy — 4 sets each, log your loads.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push compound — trains the pecs, anterior delt, and triceps through a full range of motion and handles the most load of any chest exercise.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide overhand grip emphasises the upper back and rear delts — the horizontal pull pattern that directly balances your bench pressing volume in this session.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle shifts loading toward the upper pecs — adding this after flat bench ensures the clavicular head receives direct stimulus for complete chest development.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that builds lat width — the wide grip emphasises the upper lat insertion and creates the V-taper silhouette through consistent hypertrophy stimulus.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: Cable fly keeps constant tension through the entire adduction arc — isolates the pec without tricep assistance, making it the best chest finisher for pure hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the horizontal pressing volume in this session and keeps your shoulder joint healthy across a 12-week program.

sessions.title: Legs Full

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary bilateral lower-body compound — trains quads, glutes, and core under heavy load through the full squat pattern, forming the foundation of lower body size.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the rectus femoris and vastus muscles through knee extension — the only quad exercise that fully shortens the muscle, making it the best isolation finisher on leg day.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris at its short head where the RDL alone cannot fully stimulate it, giving complete hamstring development.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core movement that trains the lower abs and hip flexors under load — included here to satisfy core volume on a lower day where trunk stability is already being tested.

sessions.title: Back & Arms
sessions.sessionFocus: Back and arms volume — hit 4 sets, control every rep.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that builds mid-back thickness through the rhomboids, traps, and teres major — the cable keeps constant tension through the full range, improving on barbell rows for hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip rotates the forearms into supination, lengthening the biceps and shifting lat emphasis toward the lower insertion — a different stimulus than the wide grip used Monday.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Incline position places the long head of the bicep in a stretched position at the start of every rep — this lengthened stimulus is one of the strongest drivers of bicep hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip shifts the load to the brachialis and brachioradialis — building these muscles under the bicep peak adds significant arm thickness that standard curls cannot deliver.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment allows the hands to spread at the bottom, fully shortening the lateral head of the tricep — the best pushdown variation for developing tricep shape and separation.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead extension pattern that loads the long head of the tricep in a stretched position — the long head is the largest of the three heads and responds best to this stretched stimulus.

sessions.title: Legs Posterior
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain volume — hamstrings and glutes, 4 sets each.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute exercise — hip thrust produces peak glute activation at the fully extended position, a stimulus the squat and hinge patterns cannot replicate, making it essential for glute hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Stiff-leg variation keeps the knees more locked than a standard RDL, increasing hamstring stretch at the bottom — a slightly different hinge stimulus from Monday that prevents adaptation stagnation.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position tilts the pelvis posteriorly, placing the hamstrings under a greater stretch than lying curls — this loaded stretch stimulus is highly effective for hamstring hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the glute medius through hip abduction — a muscle the hip thrust does not fully train, and one responsible for hip width and lateral glute development.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Straight-knee position maximally recruits the gastrocnemius, the largest calf muscle — direct plantar flexion work is the only way to develop lower leg mass.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core movement — rolling out challenges the entire anterior chain to resist spinal hyperextension, building the deep core strength that supports all your heavy compound lifts.

exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push compound — trains the pec major, anterior delt, and triceps together and anchors the session's overall chest volume.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle shifts load onto the clavicular head of the pec major — a region that flat pressing underloads and that adds visible upper chest fullness.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Cable tension stays constant through the full range of motion — this maximises pec stretch and contraction in a way dumbbell flyes can't match.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width — compound pressing alone does not develop this head adequately.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Provides anterior delt volume through a cable that maintains tension at the top of the movement, filling in the front delt stimulus without overhead pressing.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: A compound tricep movement that trains all three heads through the full press range — direct carryover to bench lockout strength and adds overall tricep mass.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a fully stretched state — the most effective position for long-head hypertrophy that pushdown variations miss.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Lateral head isolation in a shortened position — complements the stretched long-head work above and rounds out full tricep development.

sessions.title: Pull Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Pull heavy — 5 sets on pull-ups, prioritise lat depth.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary vertical pull — trains lat width and scapular depression under load with a full range of motion that most machine alternatives can't replicate.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: The wide overhand grip targets the upper back and posterior shoulder while the heavy horizontal pull adds mid-back thickness that vertical pulls alone won't deliver.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Close Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: A second vertical pull angle using a close grip shifts the stimulus toward the lower lat fibres — reinforcing the lat-width priority with accumulated volume at a moderate load.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Cable tension through a full horizontal row builds mid-back thickness while allowing a stretch at the front that free-weight rows compress out of the movement.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the lat through shoulder extension with the elbow locked — removes bicep contribution entirely and forces the lat to work alone, a key tool for the lat-width priority.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle places the long head of the bicep in a stretched position at the start of every rep — the most effective stimulus for long-head thickness and peak development.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip shifts emphasis onto the long head and brachialis — adds overall arm size and complements the supinated curl stimulus with a different force angle.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Cable behind the body extends the shoulder and places the long head under maximal tension throughout the curl — the priority long-head bias exercise for this session.

sessions.title: Legs Full (Quad Focus)

exercises.name: Back Squat

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hack Squat

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — targets the biceps femoris and semitendinosus in a way the RDL hip hinge pattern cannot fully reach.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Direct quad isolation at the knee joint — finishes quad work with a high-rep pump that compounds squats and hack squats do not fully achieve for the rectus femoris.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core movement that trains the rectus abdominis and deep stabilisers under full spinal load — demanding enough to drive adaptation in an advanced lifter.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core movement that targets the lower abdominals and hip flexors through a long lever — complements the anti-extension rollout with a different stress pattern.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Upper volume — accumulate reps on chest, back, and arms.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound on the volume day — slightly lighter than Monday's flat bench but keeps the clavicular head as the priority target across the week.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Fly-pattern machine that keeps constant tension across the pec throughout the full adduction arc — a high-rep finisher that maximises chest pump after the pressing compound.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Semi-supinated EZ grip reduces wrist strain while still loading the long and short head — adds bilateral curl volume as the second bicep session of the week.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Repeated from the pull day to reinforce the long-head priority — the stretched position at the bottom of every rep is the highest stimulus for the long head and warrants frequency.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Long-head dominant tricep movement performed with the arm overhead at the bottom position — complements the pushdown and overhead extension work from Monday with a heavier loaded stretch.

sessions.title: Lower Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior-chain volume — hamstrings and glutes, 5 sets each.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute compound of the session — the horizontal load vector maximises glute activation at full hip extension in a way vertical-load squats cannot match.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: A hip hinge with minimal knee bend that keeps the hamstrings under near-constant tension — distinct from the RDL used Wednesday and accumulates posterior-chain volume on the second lower day.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip slightly flexed, which places the hamstring in a longer muscle length than the lying version — research suggests this is the superior position for hamstring hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge with cable resistance — the forward pull of the cable increases stretch on the glutes and hamstrings at the bottom compared to free-weight hinge alternatives.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius through hip abduction — an isolation movement that compound exercises consistently underload and that directly contributes to glute width and pelvic stability.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee extended during a standing raise maximises gastrocnemius involvement — the larger of the two calf muscles and the primary target for calf size.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee flexion in the seated position de-activates the gastrocnemius and isolates the soleus — a deeper, flatter muscle that only the seated variation adequately targets.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core movement that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers against lateral force — a different stress pattern to the flexion and anti-extension work done on Wednesday.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Second appearance of the lat isolation movement this week — reinforces the lat-width priority with a high-rep pump set that fully separates bicep contribution from the lat stimulus.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Fly-pattern machine that keeps constant tension across the pec throughout the full adduction arc — a high-rep finisher that maximises chest pump after the pressing compound.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Semi-supinated EZ grip reduces wrist strain while still loading the long and short head — adds bilateral curl volume as the second bicep session of the week.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Repeated from the pull day to reinforce the long-head priority — the stretched position at the bottom of every rep is the highest stimulus for the long head and warrants frequency.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Long-head dominant tricep movement performed with the arm overhead at the bottom position — complements the pushdown and overhead extension work from Monday with a heavier loaded stretch.

days.title: Lower Volume
days.sessionFocus: Posterior-chain volume — hamstrings and glutes, 5 sets each.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute compound of the session — the horizontal load vector maximises glute activation at full hip extension in a way vertical-load squats cannot match.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: A hip hinge with minimal knee bend that keeps the hamstrings under near-constant tension — distinct from the RDL used Wednesday and accumulates posterior-chain volume on the second lower day.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip slightly flexed, which places the hamstring in a longer muscle length than the lying version — research suggests this is the superior position for hamstring hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge with cable resistance — the forward pull of the cable increases stretch on the glutes and hamstrings at the bottom compared to free-weight hinge alternatives.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius through hip abduction — an isolation movement that compound exercises consistently underload and that directly contributes to glute width and pelvic stability.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee extended during a standing raise maximises gastrocnemius involvement — the larger of the two calf muscles and the primary target for calf size.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee flexion in the seated position de-activates the gastrocnemius and isolates the soleus — a deeper, flatter muscle that only the seated variation adequately targets.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core movement that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers against lateral force — a different stress pattern to the flexion and anti-extension work done on Wednesday.
